reasoning: For _fused_moe_kernel, SM throughput is 91.96% of peak and roofline Compute SOL is 92.0%, while DRAM throughput is only 42.13% (Memory SOL 42.1%). Warps active is 100% and issue utilization is 100%, so the dominant limit is arithmetic throughput rather than memory bandwidth or occupancy.

root_causes.cause: Heavy FP32 vector ALU workload from fully fused FC1 + SiLU + FC2 path saturates VALU pipelines.

evidence.interpretation: Compute pipeline is already close to peak sustained throughput.

fixes.fix: Reduce FP32 ALU pressure by using lower-precision math where acceptable (e.g., bf16/fp16 accumulations for selected paths) and/or enabling matrix-core/Triton dot paths for GEMM-like sections.
fixes.rationale: Lower-precision or matrix-core execution increases effective math throughput and can move the kernel away from VALU saturation.

root_causes.cause: Non-tensorized reduction style (`tl.sum` over BLOCK_K/BLOCK_J with scalar/vector ops) leaves peak matrix throughput untapped.

evidence.interpretation: No tensor/matrix pipeline usage; all math is on standard ALUs.

fixes.fix: Restructure FC1/FC2 inner products into tile-wise matmul patterns (`tl.dot`/MFMA-compatible blocking) and retune BLOCK_K/BLOCK_J/BLOCK_OUT for matrix instruction mapping.
fixes.rationale: Mapping reductions to matrix instructions raises compute throughput ceiling beyond current non-tensor ALU limit.
